newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to close 5-and-10s, change name.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to close 5-and-10s, change name.

text.p: Woolworth Corp. on Thursday announced plans to close its more than 400 5-and-10-cent stores in the United States, exiting a 117-year-old business in favor of its more successful specialty athletics format.
The company, named for founder Frank W. Woolworth, also said it would change its corporate name to better reflect its global specialty retailing formats. A new name will be announced later this year.

"This company has invested significant resources in trying to revitalize the F.W. Woolworth chain," Woolworth Chief Executive Roger Farah said in a statement, but "it became clear that F.W. Woolworth would be unable, in the foreseeable future, to return to profitability as well as meet our minimum performance standards."
The retailer said it would convert about 100 of its U.S. general merchandise stores into Foot Locker, a new larger Champs Sports, or other athletic or specialty formats.
It said it would close or sell the remaining 300 general merchandise stores as well as its distribution center in Denver, Pa.
Woolworth said it expects to record an after-tax charge of $223 million, or $1.66 per share, in the second quarter in connection with the store closings and conversions.
Woolworth said it expects the restructuring to generate positive cash flow over the next two years through real estate conversions and dispositions.
The store closings will occur over the next several months, it said. The company plans sales of all store merchandise and store fixtures at cut prices.
